speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: asked	the Prime Minister (a) how many financial institutions have been investigated from 2013 to 2016 for bypassing loan restrictions on motor vehicles; and (b) whether there are any plans to tighten the regulations to effectively authenticate the purchase price of motor vehicles stated in the loan agreements.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung) (for the Prime Minister)
text: They have in place policies and procedures to do so.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung) (for the Prime Minister)
text: These procedures include obtaining multiple motor vehicle valuations from independent sources and comparing them against price lists published by authorised dealers.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung) (for the Prime Minister)
text: As part of MAS' ongoing supervision, MAS monitors FIs' compliance with rules and regulations, including through onsite inspections.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung) (for the Prime Minister)
text: It is also in the interest of an FI to ensure that motor vehicles are appropriately valued so that loans are adequately collateralised and comply with MAS' financing rules.

speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (Mr Ong Ye Kung) (for the Prime Minister)
text: However, where an FI is found in breach of any of our regulations, MAS will not hesitate to take regulatory action.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: From 26 May this year, MAS stated that the revised loan-to-value ratio and loan tenures will be extended to motor vehicle financing on a hire-purchase basis.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: Prior to the latest set of regulations, it was widely reported that MAS' curbs of 2013 were being breached quite blatantly in the motor industry by way of overtrade, disguised leases and various other inflationary strategies and creative measures.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: Can the Acting Minister clarify if companies that advertise "private-hire purchase" schemes, the hyphenation being between "private" and "hire", or with loans which are sold as "own a car with 10% downpayment", are in breach of MAS' latest guidelines?

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: The second question is, has MAS considered reviewing the inclusion of motor loans in the Total Debt Servicing Ratio (TDSR) framework, in view of the loopholes that seem to govern MAS' rules on motor vehicle financing?

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: On the first question, I thank the Member for highlighting this.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: This comes under the Ministry of Trade and Industry (MTI), who is the regulator.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: They will monitor these and take enforcement actions should they be breached.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: If I heard the Member correctly, he mentioned about private-hire vehicles.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Therefore, because it is revenue-generating, it comes under a separate consideration as if you are funding a business.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: That is why it is not captured under this policy.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: I am afraid I do not have the exact information, but I believe motor vehicle loan financing is part of the calculation in TDSR.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: The issue now appears to be focused on hire-purchase agreements which are found in the market.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: And what has happened is that while, indeed, they are set up ostensibly for a business or commercial purpose, there is also the prospect of not running it for that purpose at all, as in, for example, you register a company or a private hire under the Uber or Grab framework but in actual fact what you are doing is you are owning a vehicle but not exactly using it for the purpose for which it is registered.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: That, in a way, is a loophole or a workaround the existing MAS curbs.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: Does MAS have any plans to address this matter?

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: If this is, indeed, the case, I think it is in violation of the spirit of the policy.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: If there is specific feedback on practices like that, do let us know.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Between MAS and MTI, we will look into it.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: I do not think it is correct for this to proceed.
